name: WeNet Runtime
description: Production-oriented end-to-end speech recognition toolkit (wenet-e2e) whose LibTorch runtime ships three self-hosted server binaries — websocket_server_main, grpc_server_main, and http_server_main — for streaming and offline ASR. Default listening port 10086 across server types, with a bundled browser web client (index.html) for the WebSocket server. No built-in authentication by default. The WebSocket/gRPC transports are largely Shodan http.html-blind and route to Censys/active-probe fingerprinting.
auth_notes: No authentication in any of the three WeNet runtime servers (websocket_server_main, grpc_server_main, http_server_main), all defaulting to port 10086. The WebSocket server streams PCM in / JSON transcript out with no credential; a static browser client (runtime/libtorch/web/templates/index.html) is provided to drive it. The gRPC server is wire-only (protobuf, Shodan-blind). The HTTP server variant accepts POSTed audio. None enforce auth — the docs present these as an open ASR demo/serving setup. WebSocket/gRPC serve no descriptive HTML landing page, so http.html/http.title markers are weak; port + protocol handshake is the reliable signal.

shodan_dorks.rationale: Port-based: WeNet's websocket_server_main binds 10086 and answers a plain HTTP GET with a WebSocket upgrade/426. Serves no descriptive HTML, so http.html dorks miss it — port + upgrade header is the reachable signal
The grpc_server_main variant on 10086 answers with HTTP/2/gRPC framing; product tag on the WeNet default port narrows to the gRPC runtime

WeNet name string in an error body, gRPC service descriptor, or the served web-client HTML on 10086; low volume, high precision. gRPC service enumeration is best confirmed via active reflection/Censys since Shodan rarely captures the protobuf body

api_paths: WS :10086 (websocket_server_main: JSON config handshake + PCM stream, partial/final decode results)
known_vulns: No built-in auth — any client reaching 10086 (WS/gRPC/HTTP) gets unlimited ASR decoding
Compute theft — no rate limiting on any runtime variant; continuous decoding jobs automatable with the bundled clients
Audio PII exfiltration — streamed/uploaded audio decoded with no consent, auth, or audit logging
gRPC server ships with no TLS by default (plaintext h2c) and, where reflection is enabled, exposes the full service descriptor to unauthenticated enumeration
HTTP server variant accepts unauthenticated audio POST with no upload size/type limits — DoS surface
Bundled web client served without access control leaks the deployment's existence and connection parameters
risk_notes: Primary attack vectors: (1) Compute theft — an open 10086 endpoint (any of the three server flavors) is free E2E ASR decoding, scriptable with WeNet's own clients. (2) Audio PII exfiltration — WeNet is common in Chinese production ASR pipelines; open endpoints transcribe sensitive audio without auth or logging. (3) gRPC exposure — plaintext h2c with optional reflection lets an attacker enumerate and invoke the Recognize RPC directly. (4) Shodan-blindness on WS/gRPC favors operator obscurity; Censys/active gRPC-reflection and WebSocket handshake probing enumerate these hosts where http.html dorks miss them. (5) The HTTP variant adds an unauthenticated, unbounded audio-upload DoS surface.
deployment_notes: LibTorch runtime built from wenet-e2e/wenet (runtime/libtorch); pre-built image wenetorg/wenet-mini:latest. Three interchangeable server binaries all default to --port 10086: websocket_server_main (streaming, with a static browser client at runtime/libtorch/web/templates/index.html), grpc_server_main (streaming RPC, plaintext h2c by default), http_server_main (offline decode). WebSocket and gRPC serve no descriptive HTML — Shodan http.html/http.title dorks largely return 0; fingerprint by port 10086 + WebSocket-upgrade/426 or gRPC/HTTP-2 framing (Censys/active-probe route). Also has ONNX/GPU (Triton) and mobile runtimes, but the LibTorch servers are the canonical exposed network surface. Common in Chinese production ASR deployments; presented in docs as an open demo/serving stack with no auth.
